newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk navy ships to visit north Cyprus this week.
newsitem.headline: Turk navy ships to visit north Cyprus this week.

text.p: Turkish navy ships are to visit northern Cyprus this week in a show of solidarity with the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state, Turkey's military chief said on Tuesday.

"Our navy ships are going to the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus on January 24," Anatolian news agency quoted General Ismail Hakki Karadayi as saying before talks with visiting Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
A military official told Reuters the vessels were likely to be a frigate and two assault boats.

Turkey has promised closer military and political links with the self-declared Turkish Cypriot republic in response to Greek Cypriot plans to install anti-aircraft missiles from Russia on the south of the island.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
Turkey, which keeps 30,000 soldiers on Cyprus, has threatened to use force to halt the deployment of the S-300 missiles. The rockets are due to be installed in 16 months.
"We are not going to wait about passively for these 16 months," Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told a meeting of his Islam-based Welfare Party.
He called on the Greek Cypriot administration, regarded internationally as the island's only government, to announce it will scrap the missile deal.
"It must be made clear that (the missiles) are not coming. If it is not made clear we will take the necessary steps," he said.
